app.title: Kueh Lapis Financial Dashboard
app.tagline: Build your financial clarity layer by layer
app.compliance_disclaimer: For learning and educational purposes only. Not financial advice, product promotion, or financial recommendation under the Financial Advisers Act (FAA).

layers.title: Layer 1: Cash Flow & Habits
layers.subtitle: Where does my money go, and what is left each month?
layers.why_we_ask: Cash flow is the bedrock layer of any financial house. Without knowing what stays in your pocket each month, long-term saving or investing is built on guesswork.

layers.title: Layer 1: Emergency Runway
layers.subtitle: How many months can I survive if income stops tomorrow?
layers.why_we_ask: An emergency runway prevents you from selling investments at a loss or falling into high-interest debt when unexpected events strike.

layers.title: Layer 2: CPF & Net Worth
layers.subtitle: What is working for me in Singapore's national social security system?
layers.why_we_ask: CPF forms a massive portion of Singaporeans' financial foundation. Understanding your OA, SA, and MA allocations lets you plan housing and retirement realistically.

layers.title: Layer 3: Desired Lifestyle
layers.subtitle: What will life cost in the future, factoring in Singapore inflation?
layers.why_we_ask: Inflation silently doubles living costs every 20-25 years. Today's $3,000 monthly spending will require significantly more in your 60s and 70s.

layers.title: Layer 4: Retirement Gap & Projection
layers.subtitle: How much lump sum do I need, and is my projected fund on track?
layers.why_we_ask: Calculating your funded percentage reveals exactly whether to boost savings, extend working years, or adjust asset allocation to retire on your terms.

cash_flow.definition: Your take-home income minus all monthly living expenses. A positive cash flow means money is left over to build savings; a negative cash flow means you are drawing down savings or taking on debt.

savings_rate.definition: The percentage of your monthly take-home pay that is saved or invested (Surplus ÷ Net Take-Home Pay). A rate of 20% or higher is considered a solid, sustainable benchmark.

emergency_runway.definition: The number of months you could pay all your essential living expenses using only your liquid savings if your income stopped today (Liquid Cash ÷ Monthly Expenses).

needs_vs_wants.definition: Needs are non-negotiable living essentials (shelter, basic food, transport, baseline health insurance). Wants are lifestyle choices (dining out, streaming, holidays, luxury items) that can be paused during hard times.

cpf.definition: Singapore's mandatory social security savings scheme funded by employers and employees to support retirement, housing, and healthcare.

cpf_oa.definition: Used for housing mortgages, approved insurance, and tertiary education. Currently earns a guaranteed 2.5% per annum interest rate.

cpf_sa.definition: Dedicated to long-term retirement savings. Currently earns a minimum guaranteed 4.0% per annum interest rate.

cpf_ma.definition: Reserved for hospitalisation expenses, approved outpatient medical treatments, and MediShield Life/CareShield Life premiums. Currently earns 4.0% interest.

cpf_ra.definition: Created at age 55 from your OA and SA savings up to the Full Retirement Sum (FRS). Powers monthly payouts under CPF LIFE from age 65 onwards.

cpf_life.definition: Singapore's national longevity annuity scheme that provides guaranteed monthly payouts for as long as you live, starting between age 65 and 70.

endowment.definition: An insurance savings plan that provides a lump sum upon policy maturity or death. Returns typically comprise a guaranteed portion and a non-guaranteed bonus.

inflation.definition: The steady increase in prices over time, eroding the purchasing power of each dollar. At a modest 3% inflation rate, $100 today buys only $55 worth of goods in 20 years.

lump_sum_needed.definition: The total capital required on your retirement date to fund all expected living expenses until your planning age, accounting for post-retirement inflation and investment returns.

funded_percentage.definition: Projected Fund ÷ Lump Sum Needed. A score of 100% means your anticipated savings and CPF will fully support your desired retirement lifestyle.

guidance.positive_cash_flow: Great news! Your monthly income exceeds your spending. This monthly surplus is the engine that will power your emergency runway and investment compounding.
guidance.neutral_cash_flow: You are breaking even right now. While you are not accumulating debt, you have no safety margin if an unexpected expense arises. Try reviewing one 'Want' category.
guidance.negative_cash_flow: Your monthly expenses currently exceed take-home pay. Don't worry—most people can fix this in one sitting by converting 1 or 2 high-cost Wants into conscious savings.
